ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and rolling (at least quarterly) screening of every general partner, limited partner, beneficial owner, and authorized signatory against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, EU retained financial sanctions lists under Gibraltar law, FATF high-risk jurisdiction statements, Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit (GFIU) national alerts, and the US OFAC SDN List as a contractual prudent measure. Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status must be declared by each beneficial owner and verified by the appointed CSP; Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) and senior management approval are required for any PEP, family member, or close associate. Screening results and CDD files must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House (The Gibraltar Registry) - Limited Partnership Name Search and Reservation Portal (www.companieshouse.gov.gi), administered by the Registrar of Companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory forms and the registered name must be rendered in the Latin alphabet. A name in a non-Latin script must be transliterated into English/Latin characters and accompanied by a certified translation. The registered name must end with 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.'; it must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or a protected corporate name in Gibraltar, and it must not contain an element implying a connection with the Crown, Her Majesty's Government, a national government, an international body, or a regulated financial activity without prior written consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a provisional refusal, the applicant may within 14 days from the notice of refusal file a written submission with alternative names using the Registry's online resubmission channel. If the Registrar issues a final refusal, a formal administrative appeal must be filed with the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the refusal notice, accompanied by the original reservation application, the refusal letter, and any consent letters obtained from affected authorities; a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar by way of judicial review under Part 54 of the Gibraltar Civil Procedure Rules 2000. Where the 30-day validity of the initial reservation expires, a new reservation application is required unless an extension was granted by the Registrar before expiry for good cause shown.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Gibraltar law requires the ELP at all times to have a registered office situated in Gibraltar, but a traditional virtual office is permissible for a low-risk trading-cards publishing ELP provided that (i) the registered office is a genuine physical address maintained by a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider, (ii) the provider acts as registered agent and maintains physical custody of the statutory registers, and (iii) no PO Box is used as the sole registered address. Fully remote virtual operation without a licensed Gibraltar agent is not permissible, and payment processors (Stripe, Authorize.Net) will in practice require a verifiable operating address and UBO documentation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk. For a 'Low_Risk_Standard' ELP with no regulated financial activity, the statistical probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Companies House or GFSC within the first 12 months of incorporation is estimated at 8-10%; the probability rises to approximately 25% if the ELP is classified as a 'relevant person' under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015, holds client money, or becomes subject to a UBO register verification exercise.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Limited Partnerships Act 2010, ss. 7-12 (formation) and s. 16 (exempted limited partnership status); Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 66) applied mutatis mutandis to the corporate general partner where relevant
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, HM Government of Gibraltar, Europort, Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP-1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) together with Form LP-1ELP (Exempted Limited Partnership Declaration) and the executed Limited Partnership Agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Exempted Limited Partnership; capital contributions are contractual only and must be recorded in the Partnership Agreement's contribution schedule; no escrow account with the Registrar is required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Subscriber General Partner hereby constitutes KY_ELP as an Exempted Limited Partnership under the Limited Partnerships Act 2010. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address of the licensed Gibraltar service provider, which is appointed resident agent. RESOLVED, that the initial limited partner's subscription is accepted and the capital contribution schedule is adopted. RESOLVED, that the General Partner appoints the Money Laundering Reporting Officer with authority to execute statutory filings, open bank accounts, and appoint auditors. RESOLVED, that the General Partner is authorised to execute the Partnership Deed and apply for all industrial and environmental licences necessary for the holographic cold-foil printing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance, Registered Office and Resident Agent Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry (online name enquiry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form LP-0 for name availability confirmation and reserve the entity name. Concurrently engage a licensed Gibraltar fiduciary or service provider to act as resident agent and provide the statutory registered office address. Obtain a signed letter of consent from the service provider and evidence that the registered office will be physically located in Gibraltar.
required_dossiers: Completed Form LP-0 (name enquiry and reservation)
Letter of consent from licensed Gibraltar resident agent/service provider
Registered office address confirmation
Corporate structure chart and officer particulars of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict or similarity, file a revised name reservation within 10 working days using the same application reference; the first name variation is processed without an additional filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar notary public and partnership legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Limited Partnership Agreement containing the ELP status election, capital contribution schedule, profit-share ratios, general partner management powers, indemnification provisions, tax-transparency election and dissolution waterfall. The agreement must be executed in wet-ink by the general partner and the initial limited partner, and notarially attested before submission to the Registry.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (LP-1 exhibit)
Schedule of initial limited partner's capital contribution
Notarial attestation of execution
Power of attorney from the limited partner if executed by an authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries any clause affecting permitted indemnities or tax-transparent profit allocation, amend the relevant article and re-execute before a notary; resubmission must occur within 5 working days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, HM Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form LP-1 together with Form LP-1ELP and the notarised Limited Partnership Agreement. Attach the reserved name certificate, registered office consent, and declarations of the general partner and limited partner. Pay the prescribed filing fee through the Registry portal and retain the receipt.
required_dossiers: Form LP-1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership)
Form LP-1ELP (Exempted Limited Partnership Declaration)
Executed and notarised Limited Partnership Agreement
Register name reservation confirmation
Certified copies of passports and proof of address for the general partner and initial limited partner
Filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or notice of incomplete filing, respond through the Companies Registry portal within 14 days; cure any missing wet-ink signature or apostille within 7 days to avoid revocation of the submitted application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Registration and ELP Status Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful determination, the Registry issues the Certificate of Registration and the separate Exempted Limited Partnership certificate. Verify that the legal form, entity name, registered office, general partner details and exemption statement are accurately recorded.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration
Exempted Limited Partnership status certificate
Registered office and resident agent acceptance letter
Registry public file excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a certificate contains a typographical or legal-form error, submit a written rectification request with the original certificate and supporting evidence within 14 days; corrected certificates are reissued within 3 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Income Tax, Social Security and Tax-Transparency Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office and Gibraltar Social Security Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Exempted Limited Partnership with the Income Tax Office to obtain a partnership tax identification number and confirm pass-through treatment. File the partnership registration declaration evidencing that no Gibraltar tax is imposed at partnership level. If the entity will have employees in Gibraltar, complete employer payroll and social security registration concurrently.
required_dossiers: Partnership tax registration declaration (GIT-101P)
Certificate of Registration of the ELP
Limited Partnership Agreement excerpt evidencing profit allocation
General partner's tax status form and passport copy
Employer social security registration form (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Income Tax Office requests an economic substance explanation for the ELP, submit a concise letter confirming that the partnership does not conduct regulated activities and derives no Gibraltar-source income; response should be made within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Statutory Registers and AML Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission supervisory oversight
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a governance minute book, establish the statutory registers (partners, general partner, charges, ultimate beneficial owners), and complete the AML/CFT risk assessment in line with the Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act. The Money Laundering Reporting Officer must be formally appointed and the annual validation filing process must be set up with the Companies Registry.
required_dossiers: Governance minute book and first partner resolutions
Statutory registers of partners, general partner and UBOs
AML/CFT compliance manual and risk assessment
Annual validation form (LP-2) pre-completion template
Bank account opening due diligence pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual validation submission is queried for incomplete UBO disclosures, file a corrective beneficial ownership return within 21 days; voluntary correction before an enforcement notice eliminates the penalty exposure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Business Licensing Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Industrial and Manufacturing Licensing Unit)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Gibraltar Business Licence for Manufacturing – Printing and Production of Collectible Trading Cards

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Registration and Screening Environmental Assessment: full EIA Report is not required for light-print operations unless annual throughput of solvent-coated cold-foil card stock exceeds 50 tonnes, in which case a Category A Full EIA is triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Gibraltar Water Pollution Act 2003: treated process wastewater must not exceed BOD 50 mg/L, COD 500 mg/L, TSS 60 mg/L and pH 6.5-8.5; VOC emissions from holographic cold-foil and coating solvents must remain below 150 mg C/Nm³; all solvent wastes must be consigned by a licensed waste carrier under the Environmental Protection Act 2006.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service covering means of escape, sprinkler coverage and fire-resisting separation for printing machinery; Building Control completion certificate for structural load of cold-foil presses; occupational clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1990 including ventilation, machine guarding and noise exposure controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, HM Government of Gibraltar – Customs and Income Tax Department (Income Tax Office), 6 Seca House, Bayside Road, Gibraltar; official government portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi (Income Tax online e-filing); corporate registry: Gibraltar Companies House (Registrar of Companies).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Engage a Gibraltar-licensed registered agent and reserve the Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) name with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies. (2) File the ELP registration statement under the Limited Partnerships Act 2020, submitting the limited partnership agreement, particulars of all general and limited partners, the Gibraltar registered office address, and a Gibraltar-resident general partner or authorized representative. (3) Upon issue of the certificate of registration, apply to the Income Tax Office for the partnership's tax reference number (TRN), i.e., the fiscal file reference. (4) Each partner liable to Gibraltar tax on Gibraltar-source income obtains an individual or company TRN; non-resident partners with exclusively foreign-source income are not required to file, but the ELP must record their allocation percentages in its administrative file. (5) Register as an importer/exporter with the Gibraltar Customs Division, obtaining a customs declarant code for raw material imports (security holographic cold foil, board, inks) and finished trading card exports. (6) If staff are engaged in Gibraltar, register as an employer for PAYE and social insurance. (7) Open the ELP bank account at a Gibraltar-licensed bank or e-money institution, completing AML/KYC on the collectible trading card publishing business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Gibraltar (not the United Kingdom) is the sole taxing jurisdiction for this structure. Pass_Through_Eligible – Gibraltar ELP is statutorily fiscally transparent under the Limited Partnerships Act 2020 and the Income Tax Act: the ELP is disregarded for income tax and each partner is assessed on its allocated share of partnership income. Territorial_Scope – Gibraltar taxes only income arising in Gibraltar; foreign-source income is outside the charge. Tax_Exempt_Zone – non-resident partners with no Gibraltar-source activity have no Gibraltar income tax, no capital gains tax (none exists in Gibraltar), no inheritance tax, and no withholding tax on distributions; the 12.5% headline rate applies only to Gibraltar-source trading income allocated to partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; ELP transparency is mandatory under Gibraltar law, and there is no statutory entity-classification election for a single-member or multi-member partnership other than the profit-allocation terms of the partnership agreement. Partnerships may elect within the partnership agreement to allocate Gibraltar-source profits under Income Tax Act s.49 treatment, with assessment on partners as if the ELP did not exist. Hybrid mismatch elections under the OECD/G20 BEPS Action 2 framework (Gibraltar Taxation (Hybrid Mismatch) Rules) are available to align Gibraltar-transparent treatment with a foreign jurisdiction that treats the ELP as opaque. Legacy Qualifying/Exempt company elections under the former Income Tax (Exemption of Companies) Regulations are closed to new registrants; the go-forward regime is territorial taxation at 12.5% with full fiscal transparency.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT / No GST / No Sales and Use Tax – Gibraltar is not part of the EU or UK VAT area and levies no general consumption tax; the sole indirect tax instruments are Customs and Excise Duties under the Customs Duties Ordinance (mostly 0% for manufactured goods, with excise duties on alcohol, tobacco and fuel) and Stamp Duty on real property and insurance. Collectible trading cards (ISIC 3240) are chargeable at 0% import duty; exports are entirely outside the Gibraltar indirect tax charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold applies in law. Every person or ELP importing goods into Gibraltar must register with the Gibraltar Customs Division regardless of turnover; no VAT/GST threshold exists because no such tax is imposed. A customs declarant code and business registration are required for the import of raw materials and the export of finished trading cards; remote sales to UK/EU consumers may separately trigger foreign VAT registration (UK VAT flat rate scheme or EU One-Stop-Shop) at destination.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping mandate exists for domestic B2B/B2C sales; standard commercial invoices satisfy record-keeping obligations. Customs import and export declarations must be filed electronically through the Gibraltar Customs e-Declaration system (single administrative document equivalent) and carry a movement reference number. Income tax self-assessment returns must be filed online via the Income Tax Office portal, and the ELP must retain transactional data for the online card sales rails (Stripe and Authorize.Net) for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable as a VAT construct – Gibraltar levies no VAT, so there is no 0% export VAT criterion and no VAT refund mechanism. For customs purposes, exports are duty-free: the ELP must lodge a valid electronic export declaration demonstrating that goods did not enter Gibraltar home use; where the ELP imported raw materials (security holographic cold foil, board, inks) under inward processing relief or duty suspension, the export declaration releases the guarantee and substantiates the relief. Because card sales to UK/EU/third-country distributors are final exports, no Gibraltar indirect tax is chargeable; buyer import VAT/customs duty is a destination-country matter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic single administrative document lodged via the Gibraltar Customs e-Declaration system, with movement reference number and customs stamp)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from Gibraltar and delivery to the consignee (collectible card distributor, fulfillment center, or end customer)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank credit advices or SWIFT MT103 confirmation issued by the Gibraltar-licensed bank or e-money institution) evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Customs Duties Ordinance, false or fraudulent export declarations attract forfeiture of goods, fines up to three times the duty value, and imprisonment up to two years; duty suspended on imported raw materials is retrospectively clawed back with interest if the corresponding export is not completed within the prescribed bond period. For income tax, if the Commissioner establishes that printing/publishing activity was performed in Gibraltar and mischaracterized as offshore, the Commissioner may reassess within six years (unlimited in fraud cases), impose penalties up to 100% of the tax underpaid, and pursue the general partner and the Gibraltar registered agent. Incorrectly claimed foreign-source characterization of distribution income also exposes licensed professionals to regulatory fines under the Financial Services and Markets Act and potential disqualification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar does not maintain a domestic central bank or a dedicated foreign-exchange administration. Currency and FX affairs are anchored by the UK Crown: the Gibraltar pound (GIP), issued by HM Government of Gibraltar under the Currency Notes Act 1934, is pegged at parity (1:1) to pound sterling, with the Bank of England as the anchor issuing institution. Prudential supervision of all banks, electronic money institutions, and payment institutions operating in Gibraltar is exercised exclusively by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) under the Financial Services Act 2019 (Gibraltar).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: GIP is fully convertible at the statutory 1:1 peg to GBP for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no exchange-control approvals, profit-remittance restrictions, repatriation hurdles, or maturity limits applicable to a Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP). Distributions to non-resident partners, capital repayments, redemption proceeds, and liquidation surpluses may be remitted freely. Practical constraints are infrastructural rather than regulatory: (i) GIP is not a SWIFT-clearing currency, so international settlement is booked as GBP at parity; (ii) Gibraltar is not SEPA-participating, so EUR and USD clearing require correspondent-bank conversion; (iii) USD card receipts from Stripe/Authorize.Net may be swept into multi-currency sub-accounts without mandatory conversion into GBP or GIP; (iv) UK-resident partners remain subject to UK taxation on their distributable share, but no Gibraltarian FX or repatriation consent is triggered.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil surrender regime. The UK Exchange Control Act 1947 was repealed in 1979 and never re-enacted in Gibraltar; no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or designated-account obligation applies to export proceeds. The ELP may retain 100% of export receipts in GBP, USD, EUR, or any other convertible currency, indefinitely. The only documentary duty is under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and the Money Laundering Regulations 2019 (Gibraltar), requiring trade contracts, commercial invoices, and GB EORI customs declarations to be available for bank and GFSC review in support of the ELP's 'Low_Risk_Standard' (ISIC 3240) AML profile.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (partner capital contributions) and Operational Account (trading, FX, payroll)
Operational Account in GBP/USD/EUR with on-line banking for trade disbursements
Capital Escrow Account and Documentary Trade Account (commercial LC issuance under UCP600)
Operational Account (multi-currency, SWIFT gpi) for outbound trade wires

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH, subject to structural pre-conditions. UK-authorised electronic money institutions (Wise, Airwallex, Ebury, Revolut Business) may service a Gibraltar ELP under the UK-Gibraltar post-Brexit financial services framework (Memorandum of Understanding, March 2019), which retains passporting of UK payment services into Gibraltar without a separate Gibraltar EMI licence. Legal and operational constraints: (i) no UK or Gibraltar EMI issues a GIP-denominated IBAN, so balances are held in GBP and converted at parity; (ii) Authorize.Net does not underwrite Gibraltar-domiciled merchants, requiring the ELP to establish a US-domiciled acquiring account (wholly-owned US subsidiary or US payment facilitator) before card receipts can be repatriated; (iii) EMIs mandate full CDD on every Limited Partner holding 10% or more and typically decline where the corporate General Partner is not the sole account signatory; (iv) the 'Low_Risk_Standard' classification for ISIC 3240 permits standard (not enhanced) CDD, enabling EMI onboarding in 3-5 business days once the partnership agreement, register of beneficial owners, and GP board resolution are delivered; (v) EMIs are a secondary rail only - they cannot issue documentary letters of credit, provide sterling cheque clearing, or hold capital escrow balances under Gibraltar trust law.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar Tier-1 banks mandate a face-to-face KYC interview for at least one natural-person signatory, customarily the individual who serves as director of the corporate General Partner or a senior officer holding a written signatory mandate. Remote opening is permitted only where: (i) a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider performs the CDD interview in person at the ELP's Gibraltar registered office and issues a regulated introducer report, or (ii) the applicant already holds a passport-rated relationship with the same banking group in the UK (e.g., Barclays UK to Barclays Gibraltar). New-to-bank ELPs without a local introducer should plan for a 6-10 week onboarding timeline, a compliance visit to the registered office, and HD video-call verification of all UBOs; strictly no remote-only account opening is permitted for the first year of operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UK management-and-control challenge: the bank queries whether the ELP is economically managed from the UK parent (GB) and demands proof of Gibraltarian management before granting full transactional limits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar partnership registration certificate; minutes of General Partner board meetings physically held at the Gibraltar registered office; executed engagement letter with a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider; a tax opinion from a Gibraltar-licensed adviser confirming the ELP's UK non-residence under the UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement; a substance report evidencing a dedicated office, a resident administrator, a Gibraltar payroll, and material decision-making at the registered office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth opacity: Limited Partners are non-resident international vehicles (including Cayman/KY exempted companies or discretionary trusts), making ultimate beneficial ownership difficult to evidence to the banking provider.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of beneficial owners (PSC) filed with the GFSC; trust deed and protector consent for any trust-held limited partnership interest; source-of-wealth statements and bank references for each Limited Partner beneficially holding 10% or more; chain-of-title documentation from the Cayman registered agent where a KY interest exists; audited financial statements of the ELP under Gibraltar GAAP; a legal opinion under the Limited Partnerships Act 2013 confirming that the requested disclosure does not breach the statutory restriction on Limited Partner participation in management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-processor aggregation conflict: high-velocity, low-value on-line card sales via Stripe/Authorize.Net are mis-screened as money-service-business activity, triggering enhanced monitoring of third-party settlement funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Stripe and Authorize.Net merchant agreements naming the ELP as merchant of record; six-month gross/net settlement reconciliation per card batch; confirmation that the processors act as designated business organisations rather than customers; the ISIC 3240 production flow (security holographic cold-foil printing) evidenced by printer contracts, substrate purchase orders, and fulfilment carrier records; a commitment to run identity verification (Jumio/Onfido) for every B2C card transaction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return / Confirmation Statement of an Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, Civil Status and Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after each registration anniversary; the return date is the ELP registration anniversary and cannot be extended.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed late fee of GBP 50 plus GBP 5 per day; if outstanding for 3 months, the Registrar gazettes a notice and strikes the ELP off 30 days later unless the return and fees are paid; dissolution follows unless restored by court order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Exempt Status / Annual Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 December of each calendar year for the following year of assessment; a nil-activity ELP remains liable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts interest at 1% per month and the Commissioner may revoke or refuse to renew the exempt-status certificate; revocation subjects Gibraltar-source profits to normal income tax and exposes the general partner to collection action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Register, maintained by the Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days after each Beneficial Ownership Register anniversary; any change, including a partnership interest transfer, must be filed within 14 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Up to GBP 10,000 civil penalty for each breach plus GBP 50 per day for continuing default; criminal offense may be committed by the general partner and each designated manager; the Registry will refuse to record the transfer until the confirmation is restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ELP Partnership Tax Return / Nil Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the issue of the return form; where no notice is served, by 31 January following the end of the annual accounting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial penalty of GBP 300 and daily default penalties after 30 days; the Commissioner may issue a best-of-judgment assessment against the ELP's general partner and collect as if it were a tax assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar Income Tax Office, Economic Substance Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the ELP financial period; a nil or outside-scope notification is still required unless the ELP is dormant and expressly excluded.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalty of up to GBP 1,000 per default, repeated daily fines for continued non-compliance, and possible escalation to GFSC enforcement; no automatic strike-off is triggered, but compliance history blocks approvals and certificate renewals.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ELP is not automatically required to file audited accounts solely because it is a partnership. An independent statutory audit is compulsory only if: (a) it has a corporate general partner that must publish audited financial statements; (b) it exceeds two of the three small-company thresholds — turnover GBP 6.5 million, balance sheet gross assets GBP 3.26 million, average employees 50; (c) the partnership agreement, lender, investor or GFSC requires audit; or (d) it is in a regulated financial-services sector.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements are prepared in accordance with Gibraltar's adopted IFRS or FRS 102 (UK-heritage GAAP); the tax-transparent ELP is nonetheless required to maintain full accrual accounting and supporting records to substantiate income allocations, payments, and partners' capital percentages.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must maintain an up-to-date Register of Beneficial Owners at the registered office. Annually, no later than 28 days after the Register anniversary, the ELP files a confirmation statement declaring the registered beneficial owners unchanged or updated. On a transfer of a partnership interest, the registered owner's details and the nature and extent of the interest are updated in the Register within 14 days, and the change return is filed with the Registry within the same 14-day period; a transfer is not effective against the Registry until the updated UBO confirmation is acknowledged.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Members) and their partnership interest percentages
Register of General Partner and limited partners (name, address, contribution, liability status)
Minute Book containing partnership resolutions and manager appointments

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 - US$9,000 for a certified audit if thresholds are triggered; US$1,800 - US$4,000 for an accountants' review of an exempted small ELP

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (Gibraltar corporation tax; the ELP is fiscally transparent, so a corporate partner is charged at 12.5% on its share of Gibraltar-source trading profits, while individual partners are subject to the progressive Gibraltar personal tax scale of 9%, 16%, and 27.5% capped at 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar operates a strict territorial source regime: non-resident partners of an ELP are assessable only on profits arising from a trade carried on in Gibraltar; profits from wholly extraneous card sales, foreign distribution, and offshore licensing royalties lie outside the tax net, with no remittance test. The ELP has no separate corporate tax identity unless the general partner makes an irrevocable election under the Income Tax Act 2010 for an ‘eligible partnership’ to be taxed as a company. No manufacturing incentive specifically applies to ISIC 3240, but qualifying cold-foil printing plant and machinery attracts a 100% first-year capital allowance; trading losses are carried forward without time limit under s.47 of the Income Tax Act 2010, so the illustrative five-year ceiling in the schema is inapplicable and the correct carry-forward horizon is unlimited.
